notes:
Lead origin: inbound self-serve signup (free credits used).

Quick summary: small-but-growing SaaS for SMB customer support automation. Fast decision cycle (team of PM + eng lead + CTO). Wants Hosted API for easiest integration and quick followups. Primary question set: how to pick between Llama/Mistral/Qwen variants (13B vs 7B vs 8B-ish families), and recommendations for cost vs quality tradeoffs for an SMB monthly spend target (~$1.5k-$3k). Interested in whether quantized variants (4-bit/8-bit) are safe for support responses and when to route to higher-quality models.

Meeting notes (3/2 initial discovery call — Morgan + Priya + LanternWay CTO - Elena Park):
- Elena: "need quality close to GPT-4 for tricky policy answers but can't carry enterprise costs" — looking for sweet spot.
- Use-case: triage + answer synthesis from internal KB + short follow-up suggestions (multi-turn chat).
- Traffic profile: 600–1,200 monthly active users, peak concurrency estimated 8–12 req/s. Typical final messages ~60–120 tokens.
- Targets: p95 latency < 400ms for small responses; p99 < 800ms acceptable for longer syntheses. Cost sensitivity: strong — want per-response cost under $0.03 on average.
- Initial models they tried locally: Llama-2-13B (good coherence but memory heavy, slow), Mistral-instruct-7B (surprisingly good instruction following, lower cost), Qwen-7B (fast but occasional domain hallucinations). They ran a 200-sample prompt bench and saw Mistral variants give best cost/quality per prompt.
- Questions raised: effect of 4-bit quantization on instruction-following and safety filters; recommended routing policy (small model for short factual lookups, bigger for multi-step synthesis); whether Redwood Hosted supports hybrid routing (auto-fallback to higher-tier model) and token-level cost breakdowns for their billing forecasting.
- Security: must pass SOC2 + SSO SAML by procurement. Data residency not strict (US preferred). Need audit logs for first 12 months.

POC plan proposed (by Redwood SE Priya): 2-week hosted API POC using Redwood credits.
- Week 1: integrate minimal client (React + backend) -> log queries, compare 3 models (mistral-instruct-7b, qwen-7b, llama-2-13b-quant) on their 500 test prompts. Capture quality labels (binary helpful/not) from CS reps.
- Week 2: enable simple routing rules: short-fact queries -> mistral-7b-quant, long-synthesis -> llama-13b-nqf (non-quantized) as fallback; measure cost and latency.
- Success criteria: model accuracy >85% on labeled set OR demonstrable cost < $0.025/response while meeting latency p95 < 400ms.

Stated blockers / procurement notes:
- Budget sign-off required from Head of Ops (approval expected early May).
- SSO configuration timing uncertain; want sample SSO manifest and minimal steps.
- Concern about hallucination rates on Qwen variants for product-policy wording — asked for guidance and eval prompts.

Action items assigned:
- Morgan: send tailored perf matrix + quote for 3 variant combos and cost projections (done 3/12; attached doc).
- Priya: prepare a small eval harness + sample prompts and default routing policy example (deliver by 3/16).
- LanternWay: provide 500 anonymized support transcripts for evaluation (in progress).
